title: London, before the storm
summary: A top-down crime spree in a city still rebuilding itself. Small crews, borrowed cars, and a lot of bad decisions.
detail: The London expansion strips the series back to period cars, tight streets, and a pre-Beatles underworld. It is less a franchise milestone than a proof of concept: the same chase loop, transplanted into a colder city.

title: Swinging London, wrong side of the river
summary: The expansion moves the clock forward and the attitude up. British cars, British gangs, and a city that never quite looks away.
detail: London 1969 leans into the visual language of the era — minis, mods, and a soundtrack of period pastiche. It remains one of the series' strangest side streets: a full GTA game built as an expansion.

game: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories
title: Victor Vance arrives
summary: A soldier returns to Vice City looking for a clean way out and finds a city that only trades in complications.
detail: Victor Vance's story is a tragedy in slow motion: family loyalty, military connections, and a drug economy that turns every favour into a debt. The game ends with him alive but compromised, which makes the opening of Vice City land harder.

game: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories
title: The Vance empire
summary: Victor builds a criminal operation out of borrowed muscle and family obligation. Every new asset comes with a new enemy.
detail: By the end of Vice City Stories, Victor controls territory, businesses, and a growing reputation. The cost is the relationship with his brother Lance and the knowledge that the city always collects. His death in the opening of Vice City is the punchline to this setup.

title: Tommy Vercetti gets out
summary: A prison sentence ends and a new one begins: a drug deal on the beach goes wrong, and Tommy has to improvise.
detail: Tommy arrives in Vice City expecting a clean handoff. The deal is ambushed, the money disappears, and the people who sent him want answers. The game's opening is a masterclass in tone: sun, neon, and immediate violence.

title: The Vercetti rise
summary: Tommy works his way through the city's power brokers, buying property and collecting enemies in equal measure.
detail: The middle act is an empire-building montage: clubs, businesses, assassination contracts, and a growing crew. Tommy's refusal to be a subordinate turns a debt into a takeover, and Vice City starts to feel like his city.

title: Lance Vance changes sides
summary: The alliance at the centre of Tommy's rise starts to fracture. Loyalty in Vice City is always a temporary arrangement.
detail: Lance's resentment and Sonny Forelli's pressure converge. Tommy's empire is strong enough to survive the city, but not strong enough to survive the people closest to it. The betrayal sets up the final confrontation.

title: The last stand at the mansion
summary: Sonny comes to collect, Lance makes his choice, and Tommy settles the debt with a very loud house call.
detail: The finale is a siege: Tommy alone against Sonny's men, with Lance on the wrong side. When it ends, Tommy is the last one standing in a mansion that now belongs to him. The city is quiet for exactly one sunset.

title: CJ comes home
summary: Five years away, a funeral, and a neighbourhood that has moved on without him. Carl Johnson returns to Los Santos.
detail: The opening of San Andreas is a homecoming story: CJ finds his mother dead, his family scattered, and the Grove Street Families losing ground. The game's first act is about rebuilding trust before it becomes about rebuilding an empire.

title: Grove Street vs the Ballas
summary: Territory, drive-bys, and a family under pressure. The neighbourhood war escalates while the people closest to CJ make other plans.
detail: The gang war is both personal and structural: the Ballas have backing, Grove has history, and the police treat the whole block as a problem to manage. CJ's loyalty is tested long before the bigger conspiracy surfaces.

title: San Fierro and the Loco Syndicate
summary: The story widens beyond Los Santos: a new city, a new garage, and a drug network with ties back home.
detail: San Fierro gives CJ a base, a cover business, and a target. The Loco Syndicate arc connects the street-level betrayal to a larger criminal supply chain, and introduces Mike Toreno as a very different kind of antagonist.

title: The Caligula's heist
summary: Las Venturas, a casino, and a plan that depends on too many people behaving predictably.
detail: The Caligula's arc is San Andreas at its most cinematic: surveillance, preparation, and a heist that becomes a power struggle between criminal organisations. It is also where the game's three-city structure pays off.

title: The homecoming
summary: Los Santos riots, old friends return, and CJ finally gets to settle the score with the people who sold out Grove Street.
detail: The final act ties the gang war, the police corruption, and the family betrayal together. CJ's return to Grove Street is not a victory lap; it is a cleanup. The last confrontation is personal, and the city keeps burning behind it.

title: Liberty City, top-down
summary: The original crime spree begins: steal cars, take jobs, and climb a ladder made of other people's mistakes.
detail: The first GTA established the template: a nameless criminal, a city grid, and a radio dial. Liberty City is the starting point, but the game quickly moves through San Andreas and Vice City, treating each as a new playground.

title: Three cities, one getaway
summary: The original game's campaign spans multiple cities and ends in the kind of chase that defined the series.
detail: GTA's structure was already episodic: jobs, betrayals, and a final run for freedom. The details are sparse by modern standards, but the rhythm — plan, drive, improvise — is recognisably the series' DNA.

title: Anywhere City
summary: A retro-futurist city, three gangs, and a protagonist with no name and no patience.
detail: GTA2 leaned into dystopia: corporations, gangs, and a city that feels permanently on the edge of collapse. The game's reputation system and gang loyalty mechanics were early attempts at the living-world design the series would later refine.

title: Claude is betrayed
summary: A bank job, a girlfriend with a gun, and a prison transport that does not go as planned. Liberty City goes 3D.
detail: The opening of GTA III is still one of the series' cleanest setups: Catalina shoots Claude, leaves him for the police, and accidentally creates a free agent. The rest of the game is Claude climbing back through Liberty City's criminal hierarchy.

title: Working for the families
summary: Claude becomes useful to the Leone family, the Triads, and everyone else with a job that needs doing.
detail: GTA III's middle act is a tour of Liberty City power: the Leone family, the Colombian Cartel, the Yakuza, and a media circus. Claude's silence makes him a perfect contractor and a complete mystery to everyone around him.

title: The Cartel war
summary: Catalina returns with a cartel, a hostage, and a very personal score to settle.
detail: The Cartel arc turns the game's opening betrayal into a full-scale war. Asuka, the Yakuza, and the Colombian Cartel all collide, and Claude becomes the one variable nobody can control. The city gets louder and more dangerous.

title: The exchange
summary: A final deal, a final betrayal, and a Liberty City that keeps running long after the credits.
detail: The ending of GTA III is deliberately cold: Claude survives, Catalina does not, and the city absorbs another story without changing its expression. It set the tone for every GTA ending that followed.

title: Niko Bellic arrives
summary: A war veteran comes to Liberty City chasing an old promise and finds his cousin's life was mostly a sales pitch.
detail: Niko's arrival is the series' most grounded opening: a cramped apartment, a cousin with debts, and a city that offers work before it offers answers. The immigrant story gives GTA IV its emotional weight.

title: Blood and debts
summary: Niko's search for the man who betrayed his unit pulls him into loan sharks, gangsters, and a war he did not start.
detail: The middle of GTA IV is a web of obligation: Roman's gambling, Dimitri's manipulations, and the gradual revelation of what happened to Niko's squad. The city's optimism curdles into something colder.

title: Deal or revenge
summary: The story's final choice is not about money or loyalty. It is about whether Niko can live with either answer.
detail: The Deal ending costs Roman his life; the Revenge ending costs Kate hers. GTA IV refuses a clean victory. Whichever path the player chooses, Liberty City keeps its ledger balanced and Niko keeps carrying the cost.

title: The diamond deal
summary: A bag of diamonds passes through too many hands, linking Niko's story to the two episodes that follow.
detail: The diamond exchange is the connective tissue of the GTA IV era: a single botched deal that pulls in the Lost MC, Gay Tony's nightlife, and Niko's own circle. It is the series' clearest example of a shared criminal ecosystem.

game: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Lost and Damned
title: The Lost MC fractures
summary: Johnny Klebitz tries to hold a motorcycle club together while its president pushes it toward a war it cannot win.
detail: The Lost and Damned is a story about loyalty in a culture that mistakes loyalty for obedience. Johnny's attempts to keep the club solvent collide with Billy Grey's recklessness, and the fallout leaves the Lost weaker and angrier.

game: Grand Theft Auto IV: The Ballad of Gay Tony
title: Nightlife on the edge
summary: Luis Lopez keeps Tony Prince's clubs running while the money, the drugs, and the Russians all want a piece.
detail: The Ballad of Gay Tony is the flashiest of the GTA IV stories and the most anxious underneath. Luis is the competent one in a room full of people who have already spent the money. The finale ties back to the diamond deal and closes the IV-era trilogy.

title: Three men, one city
summary: Michael is bored, Franklin wants more, and Trevor is a live grenade with a driver's licence. Los Santos brings them together.
detail: GTA V opens with a North Yankton heist and then jumps forward to a sunlit Los Santos where Michael's retirement is falling apart. Franklin's ambition and Trevor's chaos turn a midlife crisis into a criminal partnership.

title: The first scores
summary: A jewellery store, a motorbike, and a plan that works just well enough to attract bigger problems.
detail: The early heists establish GTA V's structure: preparation, crew choice, and improvisation. Franklin's first jobs with Michael turn into a partnership, while Trevor's presence makes every plan less stable and more profitable.

title: Trevor finds out
summary: The past catches up with Michael in the most volatile way possible: Trevor learns the truth about North Yankton.
detail: Trevor's discovery reframes the entire story. Michael's retirement was built on a lie, and the reunion becomes a hostage situation with old friends. The game's tone shifts from satire to something more personal and dangerous.

title: The agency years
summary: The trio become assets for people with badges, budgets, and no intention of sharing the credit.
detail: The FIB and Merryweather arcs turn the crew into deniable contractors. Every favour creates a new liability, and the line between criminal and government work becomes a joke the characters stop laughing at.

title: Three ways out
summary: The final choice is a menu of betrayals: kill Trevor, kill Michael, or refuse the script entirely.
detail: GTA V's three endings are a commentary on the series itself. Ending A and B kill a protagonist; Ending C lets the trio survive by turning on their handlers. The last option is the most satisfying and the least realistic, which is exactly the point.

title: Jason and Lucia
summary: A new state, a new pair of protagonists, and a Bonnie-and-Clyde premise set against modern Leonida.
detail: The revealed premise follows Jason and Lucia through a version of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. The tone is modern, sunlit, and tense: a relationship story wrapped around a crime spree. Specific plot details are intentionally left out here rather than invented.

title: The state of Leonida
summary: Causeways, wetlands, small towns, and a neon capital. The map is a state, not just a city.
detail: Leonida expands the Vice City idea into a whole peninsula: Port Gellhorn's docks, Grassrivers' wetlands, Mount Kalaga's ridges, and the Keys' island roads. It is the broadest Rockstar map yet, and the setting is the story's co-star.

title: The next score
summary: A partnership, a state full of opportunities, and the oldest question in the series: how much is enough?
detail: The central tension of the revealed premise is trust: two people trying to build something together in a place designed to separate them. Everything else — the cars, the clubs, the coastline — is the scenery around that question.

title: A world that keeps moving
summary: The series' next era is built around a living state: traffic, weather, wildlife, and a news cycle that never quite looks away.
detail: Rockstar's pitch for GTA VI is density: a world with more systems, more interiors, and more ways for a plan to go sideways. The story is only one thread in a state that keeps generating its own.
